title: The vault at the end of the world
text: Drilled {{1}} a frozen mountainside on a Norwegian island halfway to the North Pole, the Svalbard Global Seed Vault {{2}} the world's insurance policy for the crops that feed us. {{3}} is designed to survive everything from rising seas to power cuts, and it is so remote and so cold {{4}} seeds stored there could outlast the institutions that deposited them. More than a million seed samples {{5}} been sent by gene banks {{6}} the world, each box a duplicate of a collection held elsewhere. In 2015, {{7}} civil war had wrecked Syria's own gene bank, researchers quietly withdrew their ancient wheat and barley samples, grew them out in Lebanon and Morocco, and restocked the vault — proof that the insurance works. {{8}} is somehow fitting that the coldest place in the seed world exists to keep the future warm.
